problem: Determine whether $v=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2-2\text{i}\end{aligned}]$ is an eigenvector of the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}-2 & -2 \\ 4 & 2\end{aligned}].$ If so, then what is the corresponding eigenvalue?
worked_solution:
The eigenvectors of $A$ are the non-zero vectors $v$ such that $Av=\lambda v.$ So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}Av & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & -2 \\ 4 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2-2\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4\text{i} \\ 4-4\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4\text{i} \\ -4{\text{i}}^{2}-4\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & =2\text{i}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2-2\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & =2\text{i}v.\end{aligned}
$$

Since $Av=2\text{i}v,$ we conclude that $v$ is an eigenvector of $A$ and the corresponding eigenvalue is $\lambda =2\text{i}.$
